assets.prompt: Use case: sketch-to-render. Create a polished orthographic overhead VTT painting by repainting the supplied 3:1 rectangular layout guide. Output a full bleed 3:1 horizontal strip. Treat guide as binding for shapes, scale and placement. This is the extreme north end of a winter mountain fortress, snowbound timber and stone in late medieval Japan. Top is north. Strictly vertical drone camera, surfaces seen from directly overhead, no horizon, no perspective. Architectural craft at tabletop miniatures scale: layered charcoal kawara ceramic roof tiles grouped in short sweeping hipped roofs, snowy windward ridges, subtle copper finials, red-lacquer gate lintel, weathered timber, carefully fitted greystone paving, charcoal arrow slits. At the precise coordinates of the reference: the long rampart fills the top 42% edge to edge. Each of the two north-south oriented rectangular gatehouse roofs flanks the open central unfurnished passage with roof footprints x36–47% and 53–64%, ending at y67% of image. The narrow central north-south passage remains exposed from the top edge down, with two distinct thin horizontal gate lines at y33% and 63%, exactly like the diagram. Narrow line of crenels and tiny weathered red pennants along outer edge of rampart at y42%. A snowy berm then a STRAIGHT horizontal frozen defensive moat (across y75%–92%) with a small center stone bridge x46–54%, aligned with passage. Pale snow at bottom edge, with only a tiny continuation of packed snowy road in the center. Rich atmospheric naturalism and restrained gouache edges, blue-gray soft winter daylight from upper left, subtle short cast shadows, dark patinated masonry, windswept cream-white snow caught on roof tiles, fine ice fractures and translucent blue ice. Restrained high-end historical fantasy battle map with lifelike material detail, no black outlines, no figures, no extra buildings or trees, no symbols, no painted grid, no text or border. Preserve margins precisely and fill the original rectangular frame.

Use case: stylized-concept. Game environment production texture atlas for a premium naturalistic hand-painted winter battlemap of feudal Japan. Exactly FOUR equally sized square material swatches, in a 2 by 2 grid filling an opaque square edge to edge, no space or frame at subdivisions. Each square is a completely continuous, seamless, homogeneous surface sampled from directly overhead at 90 degrees under cool overcast daylight. No horizon, depth of field, scale bars, text, objects, dramatic shadows or obvious tile-size motifs. Upper left: quiet powder snow field, warm ivory high ridges, cool blue gray hollows, subtle windcombed sastrugi in tiny tufts and scatterings of ice crystals. Upper right: the close surface of an entire packed snowy road, frost over weathered ochre-grey grit and earth, a few tiny pebbles and compressed crystalline patches, continuous road material over the entire square, NO road edges or track boundaries. Lower left: woodland ground after snowfall, mostly soft pearl gray snow with tiny low-contrast patches of brown pine needles, twigs and translucent fine grass poking through; no trunks/trees or boulders. Lower right: continuous frozen pale arctic teal water with milky blue irregular platelets, branching hairline fissures, submerged long bubbles and light frosted snow dust. Each swatch is richly observed and natural, delicate cold colors, top-down digital gouache with the material accuracy of a nature study. Details appropriate for an 8-metre field of view for EACH square. All four swatches quadrants exact 50%. No type or labels.

Use case: stylized-concept. TOP MIDDLE: a second natural Japanese black pine crown seen DIRECTLY above, distinct ragged, denser splayed evergreen boughs with small pillows of windblown snow, muted sage pine needles and occasional ochre dead tips. Use case: stylized-concept. Create a NEW transparent RGBA game asset atlas containing nine distinct snow-covered tree canopies, to supplement the supplied reference sheet's top row. The reference is a style and camera reference only. Use a perfectly regular 3 by 3 square atlas; one isolated canopy centered at its trunk in each cell with generous transparent gutters (at least 9% clear on each side). ALL NINE trees are seen directly vertically down along the trunk from an overhead orthographic tabletop camera. Snowy late medieval Japanese woodland; naturalistic detailed painterly spruce, pine and deciduous branching like the reference. Lock lighting direction across EVERY cell: soft cool highlights toward TOP LEFT and gentle internal shading toward BOTTOM RIGHT. Keep this orientation fixed throughout; vary branch architecture, branching at gaps, crown proportions and snow clump distribution instead. No cast shadow outside the canopy, no ground or background. Top row: lush broad blue spruce; spindly uneven spruce with wide gaps; round dense layered dark spruce. Middle row: old Japanese black pine with a broad lobed canopy; younger wind-pruned Japanese pine with visible radial structure; low irregular spreading pine with thinner needle clusters and scattered snow patches. Bottom row: bare silver birch with many fine branches; frost-dusted short oak with an irregular open fork structure; airy leafless maple with widely spaced crooked limbs and twigs. Snow looks settled in place, evergreen needles muted dark greens, fine branch detail and no exaggerated perspective. Forms are readable at tabletop token scale. Only these nine separate objects, on actual transparency, no extraneous objects, no text, no grid lines, no backdrop.
